meta.title: Image Cropper
meta.description: Dual coordinate spaces, eight-handle drag with aspect ratio enforcement, rule-of-thirds overlay, and offscreen canvas export at full image resolution.

blocks.content: Image cropping looks simple until you build it. The image must be scaled and centered to fit whatever container you give it. Drag deltas arrive in display pixels but the crop region lives in image pixels — those two spaces must stay in sync as the container resizes. Eight handles plus a move zone all share one pointer handler. Aspect ratio enforcement has different logic for corner vs edge drags. And the final export must run at the original image resolution regardless of how small the preview is on screen.

CropperRoot owns all of it. Pass src and onCrop — the default layout renders a toolbar with aspect ratio presets, a canvas with the overlay, and a live preview panel. Pass children to compose your own layout using the same useCropper hook.

blocks.title: CORS requirement
blocks.content: Images loaded from a different origin must respond with Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers. CropperCanvas already sets crossOrigin="anonymous" on the img element — the server must allow it or the canvas export will throw a security error.
Drag the handles to resize the crop region. Drag inside the region to move it. Use the aspect ratio presets in the toolbar, then click Crop to export.
Pass src and onCrop. The default layout — toolbar, canvas, preview — renders automatically.

Pass defaultAspectRatio to lock the initial region. The user can still switch via the toolbar. Setting a fixed ratio constrains all eight handles consistently — corners are width-primary, edge handles re-center the opposite axis.

blocks.code:
<CropperRoot
  src={src}
  config={{
    defaultAspectRatio: "16:9",
    outputFormat: "image/jpeg",
    quality: 0.88,
  }}
  onCrop={handleCrop}
/>

blocks.title: Programmatic ratio control
blocks.content: Call setAspectRatioPreset from useCropper to switch the ratio from outside the toolbar — useful when you want ratio controls inline with the rest of your form.
Pass children to CropperRoot to replace the default layout entirely. All sub-components still read from context via useCropper.
Access the full crop state and actions anywhere inside CropperRoot. Useful for wiring a custom Crop button, reading the current region dimensions, or triggering export from outside the toolbar.

blocks.content: The system maintains two coordinate spaces. Image space is the coordinate system of the original image in pixels — CropRegion always lives here, and so does the canvas export. Canvas space is the display pixel space inside the container after the image has been scaled to fit. computeTransform() derives a scale factor and centering offsets each time the container resizes via ResizeObserver. Drag deltas arrive in canvas space and are divided by scale before being applied to the region, so drag feel is consistent at any container size.

The entire overlay is one SVG element. On pointerdown, hitTest() checks the pointer position against eight handle rects and the interior move zone — no per-handle event listeners. setPointerCapture() on the SVG ensures pointermove and pointerup arrive even if the cursor leaves mid-drag. Drag state is stored in a ref, not useState, so the pointer move handler does not trigger a re-render on every pixel — only the region state update does.

Aspect ratio enforcement runs after the edge deltas are applied. Pure-horizontal drags (east/west only) recompute height from the new width and re-center vertically. Pure-vertical drags recompute width and re-center horizontally. Corner drags treat width as primary and derive height. A second clamp pass after AR adjustment keeps the entire region inside image bounds.
